definition: Pooling layers downsample each feature map in the network, reducing the dimensions and allowing for assumptions to be made about features contained in the sub-regions binned.
details: Pooling layers downsample each feature map in the network, reducing the dimensions and allowing for assumptions to be made about features contained in the sub-regions binned. Max pooling and average pooling are techniques to perform this downsampling by taking the maximum and average value, respectively, in each patch of the feature map.

explainer.lead: Pooling layers shrink each feature map so the network carries fewer dimensions and can generalise about features within small sub-regions. Max pooling and average pooling are the two standard ways to perform that downsampling.

tiers.eli5: Imagine summarising a photo by covering it with small squares and keeping one number per square: the biggest in the square (max) or the typical one (average).
tiers.practitioner: Engineers insert pooling between convolution blocks to cut spatial size, cost and sensitivity to small shifts; a common pitfall is over-pooling, which throws away location detail needed for fine-grained tasks.
tiers.paperLevel: Each feature map is divided into patches; max pooling outputs the maximum value in each patch and average pooling outputs the mean, reducing the map's dimensions. Both discard the exact positions of values within a patch.

explainer.example: On a 4x4 feature map with 2x2 pooling, a patch holding 1, 3, 2, 4 becomes 4 under max pooling and 2.5 under average pooling, giving a 2x2 output.
